justification: The only human genetic evidence is the 10p15.3 subtelomeric deletion series (PMID 22847950), which reports neurodevelopmental features (cognitive/behavioral/developmental differences, speech and motor delay, hypotonia, seizures) and nominates ZMYND11 and DIP2C as candidates; however, these are multigene copy-number deletions that cannot single out ZMYND11, and autism spectrum disorder is not explicitly diagnosed in the cohort, so this cannot support "Established" and only weakly supports "Existing." The remaining articles (PMIDs 24590075, 24963723, 24732008, 25097667) are purely molecular/structural studies of ZMYND11 as an H3.3K36me3 reader, transcription elongation co-repressor, tumour suppressor, and a bromodomain FRAP assay target, with no autism relevance beyond the general plausibility that chromatin-regulator haploinsufficiency causes neurodevelopmental disease. No article reports ZMYND11 point mutations or sequence variants in autism probands, and no replication exists across independent patients. Therefore the evidence sits mostly between a biologically plausible (chromatin regulator, candidate within a neurodevelopmental deletion region) hypothesis and a limited human association.
